note: The ns-clause and declaration surfaces, each measured on the corpora before the fix. D5: `:only` is `:refer`'s legacy twin and its name list is a LIST — `(:use [clojure.java.browse :only (browse-url)])`, 16 sites in the clojure corpus alone — so it registered no refer name and every call dangled. D5c: the libspec guard looked only at a LIST parent, so a name list nested in a VECTOR spec walked as CODE and fabricated a top-level call; once D5 taught the handler to read `:only` that fabrication acquired a lib (`ns -[calls]-> clj.java.browse/browse-up`, isTopLevel). D6: `(declare a b)` interns a var, but `declare` is a core form, so it produced no symbol and no edge AND its names were not in-file declarations — 68 sites — leaving every later call with nothing to resolve to. D8: `:rename {old new}` was a declared limitation (F17); measured at 7 sites in clj-kondo and closed. The pairing is POSITIONAL — a map literal alternates key/value, so the NEW name is the ODD child; reading both would make the unbound `old` name resolve, which is the shadowing `:rename` exists to prevent. `uses-rename -> rewrite-text` is therefore pinned as a BARE dangling target: Clojure really does unbind that name, so a call to it is a genuine unresolved var and the analyzer must not invent a lib for it.
